shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures rose for a second straight session on Thursday, tracking a rally in oil prices and gains in Asian shares.($1 = 158.8300 yen)($1 = 6.6752 yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures rose for a second straight session on Thursday, tracking a rally in oil prices and gains in Asian shares.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for May delivery
was up 3.5 yen, or 0.83%, at 426.8 yen ($2.69) per kg as of 0152 GMT
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 155 yuan, or 0.84%, to 18,565 yuan ($2,781.19) per metric ton
The most active January butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) climbed 390 yuan, or 2.63%, to 15,235 yuan per metric ton
Rubber price moves over the past week were driven mainly by macroeconomic factors, with fundamentals largely unchanged, analysts from broker Zijin Tianfeng Futures said in a note
Asian shares eked out a rare rally on Thursday after Wall Street fought back from deep lows, with Japan's Nikkei
Stronger risk sentiment tends to support rubber futures
Crude oil prices rallied on Wednesday after Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked ​Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, raising concerns about unexpected Middle East supply disruptions
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil
The overall supply situation remains tight, with rubber imports at low levels, the analysts said
They added that Hainan's production area has entered a seasonal output reduction phase, and some farms in Yunnan province have stopped tapping

Vietnam's natural rubber exports fell about 10.5% in the first 10 months to 520,000 tons, from 581,000 tons a year earlier, according to Reuters calculations based on data from rubber information provider Qinrex
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for February delivery (STFG7) last traded at 237.3 US cents per kg, up 2.3%
